about.summary_academic:
Before I started my professional career, it all began in college. That’s where I wrote my first “Hello World” program in Java using Eclipse. It might sound like just another line of code, but I remember the thrill of seeing a program I’d created myself (even though it gave me a headache, haha) make me feel proud. From that moment on, I developed small applications—such as a calculator, among others—first in Eclipse and later in NetBeans.

As my studies progressed, I discovered a whole new world: databases. I learned to work with MySQL from the command line—without a graphical interface—by writing SQL queries and understanding how information could be stored, related, and retrieved. Shortly after, PHP, HTML, and CSS came along, and that’s when everything started to make sense: connecting an application to a database to build dynamic systems. Those interfaces that gradually came to life are what helped me discover that I enjoyed building user experiences and that web development was a path I wanted to continue exploring… and one that, to this day, I still enjoy.

College also allowed me to experiment with other technologies. I developed small mobile apps using Android Studio, first by creating interfaces entirely in XML and later by using the visual editor (drag-and-drop). I also had the opportunity to work with Ionic to learn about hybrid mobile development.

Not everything revolved around web development. In some courses, I explored Python and took my first steps in data analysis using the Pandas library. Although it was just an introduction at the time, that knowledge has since sparked my interest and is part of the path I’m following toward a career in Data Engineering.

I also learned how to work with Arduino. Building small circuits on a breadboard, controlling LEDs, and seeing how the software interacted with the hardware gave me a completely different way of understanding programming and allowed me to appreciate the versatility of this profession.

Last but not least, I took my first steps in Linux with the Ubuntu distribution and learned how to use the terminal with basic commands. Although these were simple tasks, that experience helped me become familiar with an environment that remains essential in software development today.

Looking back, I realize that none of those technologies were a waste of time. Each one taught me a different way to solve problems and broadened my perspective on software development. Some have become part of my daily routine, while others simply piqued my curiosity, but all of them helped lay the foundation on which I continue to build my career.
about.summary_professional:
It all started with WordPress web development. I began by working with visual builders, and over time, I moved on to customizing themes and plugins using code, optimizing websites, and deploying them to production.

This experience allowed me to participate in projects for various clients and collaborate closely with senior developers, designers, and project managers. As a result, I strengthened skills such as communication, teamwork, and the ability to analyze and solve problems both during development and once projects were in production. In addition, I have had the opportunity to work both remotely and in person, adapting to different ways of collaborating.

I enjoy web development and remain open to new projects in this field. At the same time, in my free time, I’ve started to delve deeper into data engineering, a field that has piqued my interest and in which I hope to continue growing professionally without neglecting my experience as a developer.
